---
title: "Cellerator"
---

Cellerator is a compiler and execution substrate for biologically structured computation. It explores how recurring relations, support patterns, and useful order can become reusable geometry and executable work while quantitative values change.

The implementation combines a host-first compiler/SDK route with a separately configured CUDA numerical runtime. It includes prepared operations and multiple physical candidates, while the wider language, general training, and adaptive execution goals remain incomplete. The dated [current snapshot](status/current.md) separates implemented, bounded, and future capabilities.

Biological semantics guide which structure may be reusable; measurements decide whether a physical realization is useful. No one sparse format or device path is the universal center. See the short [design overview](design/overview.md), then the detailed architecture and subsystem chapters below.

## Governing rule

Cellerator should preserve biological meaning when that meaning helps execution, but performance decides the representation.

Every additional layer must reduce time, traffic, synchronization, communication, or downstream cost. Otherwise it is decorative weight.
